work_relations.note: Like many Impressionists, Monet was influenced by Japanese Ukiyo-e prints. Hokusai's series, depicting a single subject under various conditions, provided a conceptual model for Monet's own serial paintings, including his views of San Giorgio Maggiore.
Hokusai's series of woodblock prints, exploring a single subject under varying conditions, is widely cited by art historians as a key precedent for Monet's serial painting method.
Hokusai's series of woodblock prints, which depicted a single subject from various viewpoints and in different conditions, is widely cited as a key inspiration for Monet's serial approach.

places.connection: Hokusai was born in Edo, which is present-day Tokyo.
Hokusai created the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series in his studio in Edo.
The museum houses a collection of Hokusai's works, including pieces from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
Mount Fuji is the central subject depicted in the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series.
Nagoya Castle is depicted in one of the prints from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series.
